contents.html: NIST hosted the sixth annual Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) Research & Development Workshop on April 17-19, 2007. The two and a half day event brought together computer security experts from academia, industry, and government to share progress, and explore challenges, in PKI and related technologies. In addition to the nine refereed papers, this proceedings captures the essence of the workshop activities including the keynote addresses, invited talks, panels, a birds-of-a-feather session and the popular informal rump session.
contents.html_ja: NIST は、2007年4月17日から19日に、第6回公開鍵基盤（PKI）研究開発ワークショップを主催しました。この2日半のイベントには、学術界、産業界、政府のコンピュータセキュリティ専門家が集まり、PKIと関連技術の進展を共有し、課題を探りました。9件の査読付き論文に加えて、本会議録には、基調講演、招待講演、パネル、バーズ・オブ・ア・フェザー・セッション、人気の非公式なランプセッションなど、ワークショップ活動の要点が収められています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p5の前書きの段落

contents.html: Continuing a trend from previous years, the workshop addressed an increasingly broad range of topics beyond PKI. The theory and practice of identity management took center stage for much of the workshop. In keeping with this year’s theme, “Applications Driven PKI”, practical applications were the focus of many presentations as well. And as always, several presentations describing innovations in infrastructure design prompted spirited discussions.
contents.html_ja: 例年の傾向が続き、今回のワークショップでは、PKI を超えるますます広い範囲の話題が扱われました。ワークショップの多くの時間で、ID 管理の理論と実践が中心となりました。今年のテーマ「アプリケーション駆動型 PKI」に沿って、多くの発表で実用的なアプリケーションも焦点となりました。そして例年どおり、インフラ設計における革新を述べたいくつかの発表が、活発な議論を呼びました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p5の前書きの段落

contents.html: The identity management theme was evident throughout the workshop, beginning with the opening keynote presentation. Carl Ellison presented on behalf of Microsoft’s Identity and Access Architect, Kim Cameron. Cameron’s seven Laws of Identity provided an excellent foundation for several subsequent presentations. Carl’s presentation was immediately followed by a panel on identity management systems, with a lively exploration of their commonalities and differences. The second keynote, by Ken Klingenstein, explored an “attribute ecosystem” where the academic community’s Shibboleth project might play a central role. A later panel discussion explored the lessons learned in identity systems that leverage both the Security Association Markup Language (SAML) and PKI.
contents.html_ja: ID 管理というテーマは、冒頭の基調講演をはじめ、ワークショップ全体を通じて顕著でした。Carl Ellison が、Microsoft の ID・アクセスアーキテクトである Kim Cameron に代わって講演しました。Cameron の「ID の 7 つの法則」は、その後のいくつかの発表の優れた基盤となりました。Carl の講演の直後には、ID 管理システムに関するパネルが行われ、それらの共通点と相違点が活発に検討されました。Ken Klingenstein による 2 つ目の基調講演では、学術コミュニティの Shibboleth プロジェクトが中心的な役割を果たす可能性のある「属性エコシステム」が探究されました。その後のパネルディスカッションでは、セキュリティアサーションマークアップ言語（SAML）と PKI の両方を活用する ID システムで得られた教訓が検討されました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p5の前書きの段落

contents.html: Applications, both deployed and in development, were also a common theme. Projects from the European Union and Argonne National Laboratories were the subject of refereed paper presentations. A panel from the mortgage industry describing PKI-based mortgage applications generated extensive discussions with its intersection of signature technologies and the legal implications. A Federal Government panel presented applications from the Treasury Department, Food and Drug Administration, and the Drug Enforcement Administration.
contents.html_ja: 導入済みのものも開発中のものも含め、アプリケーションも共通のテーマでした。欧州連合とアルゴンヌ国立研究所のプロジェクトが、査読付き論文の発表の題材となりました。PKI ベースの住宅ローンのアプリケーションについて述べた住宅ローン業界のパネルは、署名技術と法的な影響が交わる点について、広範な議論を生みました。連邦政府のパネルでは、財務省、食品医薬品局、麻薬取締局のアプリケーションが紹介されました。

contents.html: Two presentations explored the intersection between applications and identity management. Yet another Federal Government panel explored the deployment of a PKI-based identity management credential, the Personal Identity Verification (PIV) Card, and the opportunities and challenges this project presents for application developers. The rump session featured a complementary presentation on PKI in Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) passports. PKI is applied to these identity credentials in entirely different ways, yet share the overall goal of identifying a credential holder.
contents.html_ja: 2件の発表が、アプリケーションとID管理の交点を探究しました。もう1つの連邦政府のパネルは、PKIベースのID管理用資格情報である個人識別検証（PIV）カードの導入と、このプロジェクトがアプリケーション開発者にもたらす機会と課題を探りました。ランプセッションでは、無線自動識別（RFID）パスポートにおけるPKIに関する補完的な発表がありました。これらの身分証明用資格情報ではPKIがまったく異なる方法で適用されていますが、資格情報の保持者を識別するという全体的な目標を共有しています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p5の前書きの段落

contents.html: New approaches to infrastructure design were also presented in the workshop. Three presentations addressed PKI for Grids, including two presentations from the United Kingdom. Other presentations included “one time private keys,” a “temporal key release infrastructure,” and a system for delegating client authenticated web access through proxy certificates. These schemes strive to establish PKI-based analogs to common practices in other arenas, such as sealed bids at auctions or password-sharing for privilege delegation.
contents.html_ja: インフラ設計への新しいアプローチも、ワークショップで発表されました。3 件の発表がグリッド向けの PKI を扱い、そのうち 2 件は英国からの発表でした。その他の発表には、「ワンタイム秘密鍵」、「時間的鍵リリースインフラ」、プロキシ証明書を通じてクライアント認証済みのウェブアクセスを委任するシステムなどがありました。これらの方式は、オークションでの封印入札や、権限委任のためのパスワード共有など、他の分野の一般的な慣行に対応する PKI ベースの方式を確立しようとするものです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p6の前書きの段落・署名

contents.html: In all, the workshop included the presentation of two invited keynote presentations, nine referred papers, five panel discussions, a rump session, and a birds-of-a-feather session. Once again, the workshop was an international event with 125 attendees representing a cross-section of the global PKI community, with presenters from the USA, United Kingdom, Israel, Singapore, Brazil, and Canada. Due to the success of this event, a seventh workshop is planned for March 4-6, 2008. Given the broad interest in identity management techniques regardless of the underlying technology, next year’s workshop will be renamed to reflect the de facto shift in focus.
contents.html_ja: 全体として、ワークショップでは、2件の招待基調講演、9件の査読付き論文、5件のパネルディスカッション、ランプセッション、バーズ・オブ・ア・フェザー・セッションが行われました。今回もワークショップは国際的なイベントとなり、世界のPKIコミュニティの各層を代表する125名の参加者があり、発表者は米国、英国、イスラエル、シンガポール、ブラジル、カナダから参加しました。このイベントの成功を受けて、第7回ワークショップが2008年3月4日から6日に予定されています。基盤となる技術にかかわらず、ID管理技術への広い関心を踏まえ、来年のワークショップは事実上の焦点の変化を反映するよう名称が変更されます。

subtitle_ja: 第6回（6th） PKI R&D ワークショップ「アプリケーション駆動型 PKI」会議録
description: 2007 年 4 月に NIST が主催した第 6 回 PKI R&D ワークショップの会議録で、公開されているのは序文などです。
series: NIST Interagency or Internal Report · PDF 原文抽出

original_blocks.html: William T. Polk Computer Security Division
Information Technology Laboratory National Institute of Standards and Technology
NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF STANDARDS AND TECHNOLOGY

Certain commercial entities, equipment, or materials may be identified in this document in order to describe an experimental procedure or concept adequately. Such identification is not intended to imply recommendation or endorsement by the National Institute of Standards and Technology, nor is it intended to imply that the entities, materials, or equipment are necessarily the best available for the purpose.

NIST hosted the sixth annual Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) Research & Development Workshop on April 17-19, 2007. The two and a half day event brought together computer security experts from academia, industry, and government to share progress, and explore challenges, in PKI and related technologies. In addition to the nine refereed papers, this proceedings captures the essence of the workshop activities including the keynote addresses, invited talks, panels, a birds-of-a-feather session and the popular informal rump session.

Continuing a trend from previous years, the workshop addressed an increasingly broad range of topics beyond PKI. The theory and practice of identity management took center stage for much of the workshop. In keeping with this year’s theme, “Applications Driven PKI”, practical applications were the focus of many presentations as well. And as always, several presentations describing innovations in infrastructure design prompted spirited discussions.

The identity management theme was evident throughout the workshop, beginning with the opening keynote presentation. Carl Ellison presented on behalf of Microsoft’s Identity and Access Architect, Kim Cameron. Cameron’s seven Laws of Identity provided an excellent foundation for several subsequent presentations. Carl’s presentation was immediately followed by a panel on identity management systems, with a lively exploration of their commonalities and differences. The second keynote, by Ken Klingenstein, explored an “attribute ecosystem” where the academic community’s Shibboleth project might play a central role. A later panel discussion explored the lessons learned in identity systems that leverage both the Security Association Markup Language (SAML) and PKI.

Applications, both deployed and in development, were also a common theme. Projects from the European Union and Argonne National Laboratories were the subject of refereed paper presentations. A panel from the mortgage industry describing PKI-based mortgage applications generated extensive discussions with its intersection of signature technologies and the legal implications. A Federal Government panel presented applications from the Treasury Department, Food and Drug Administration, and the Drug Enforcement Administration.

Two presentations explored the intersection between applications and identity management. Yet another Federal Government panel explored the deployment of a PKI-based identity management credential, the Personal Identity Verification (PIV) Card, and the opportunities and challenges this project presents for application developers. The rump session featured a complementary presentation on PKI in Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) passports. PKI is applied to these identity credentials in entirely different ways, yet share the overall goal of identifying a credential holder.

New approaches to infrastructure design were also presented in the workshop. Three presentations addressed PKI for Grids, including two presentations from the United Kingdom. Other presentations included “one time private keys,” a “temporal key release infrastructure,” and a system for delegating client authenticated web access through proxy certificates. These schemes strive to establish PKI-based analogs to common practices in other arenas, such as sealed bids at auctions or password-sharing for privilege delegation.

In all, the workshop included the presentation of two invited keynote presentations, nine referred papers, five panel discussions, a rump session, and a birds-of-a-feather session. Once again, the workshop was an international event with 125 attendees representing a cross-section of the global PKI community, with presenters from the USA, United Kingdom, Israel, Singapore, Brazil, and Canada. Due to the success of this event, a seventh workshop is planned for March 4-6, 2008. Given the broad interest in identity management techniques regardless of the underlying technology, next year’s workshop will be renamed to reflect the de facto shift in focus.
